examples.en: He took part in the war at nineteen.
Before going to war, he left a letter to his family.
Our country was also asked to join the war.
It is a day to honor the soldiers who fought in the war.
It is a story of people who went abroad and fought in the war.
They say he agonized for a long time over whether to join the war.

explain: '전쟁에 참전하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 함께 써요. 일반 대회나 행사에는 '참가하다', '참여하다'를 써요. 이미 전쟁이라는 뜻이 들어 있어서 '전쟁에'를 빼도 말이 통해요.

phrases.en: The soldiers who fought in the war returned home.
phrases.nuance_ko: '참전하다'를 과거 관형형으로 바꿔 사람을 꾸미는 쓰임이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past modifier form, used to describe a person.

phrases.en: Our country did not take part in that war.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전쟁에 나가지 않았다는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, meaning not joining a war.
phrases.en_equiv: not to take part in war

phrases.example: 그는 어쩔 수 없이 참전하게 되었어요.
phrases.en: He had no choice but to end up joining the war.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게 되다'로 자기 뜻과 상관없이 전쟁에 나가게 된 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-게 되다' describes ending up joining a war as circumstances developed.
phrases.en_equiv: to end up joining the war

explain_en: Take part in a war as a soldier. Used with the particle '에', as in '전쟁에 참전하다'. For ordinary contests or events, use '참가하다' or '참여하다'. Since the idea of war is already inside the word, it still works even if you drop '전쟁에'.

en: to spread outward; to have a ripple effect

examples.en: It was a small accident, but its effects spread across the country.
Exchange rate changes spread their effect to small and medium businesses too.

examples.ko: 그 소식이 퍼지면서 불안감이 시장에 파급되었어요.
examples.en: As the news spread, anxiety spread through the market.

examples.ko: 이 정책이 어디까지 파급될지 아직 몰라요.
examples.en: We don't know yet how far this policy's effects will reach.

examples.ko: 유행이 다른 나라로 파급되는 데 오래 걸리지 않았어요.
examples.en: It didn't take long for the trend to spread to other countries.

examples.ko: 문제가 파급되기 전에 빨리 막아야 해요.
examples.en: We have to stop the problem quickly before it spreads.

explain: 영향, 효과, 충격이 다른 곳으로 퍼져 나갈 때 쓰고, 뉴스나 경제 이야기에서 많이 나와요. '퍼지다'보다 딱딱하고, 보통 '파급 효과'나 '영향이 파급되다'로 말해요.

phrases.example: 이 정책은 다른 산업에 미치는 파급 효과가 커요.
phrases.en: This policy has a big ripple effect on other industries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영향이 넓게 퍼질 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for effects that spread widely.
phrases.en_equiv: to have a big ripple effect

phrases.example: 이 문제가 다른 나라로도 파급될 것 같아요.
phrases.en: This problem seems likely to spread to other countries too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 영향이 퍼질 거라고 예상할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to predict that an impact will spread.

phrases.example: 가격 인상의 영향이 시장 전체로 퍼져 나갔어요.
phrases.en: The effect of the price rise spread through the whole market.
phrases.nuance_ko: '파급되다'보다 부드럽고 일상 대화에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer, more everyday way to say it.

explain_en: It is used when an influence, effect or shock spreads to other places, and is common in news and economic talk. It is stiffer than '퍼지다', and usually appears as '파급 효과' or '영향이 파급되다'.

en: to return; to restore; to give back

examples.en: The company gives its profits back to society.

examples.ko: 그 부자는 재산을 사회에 환원하기로 했어요.
examples.en: That rich man decided to give his wealth back to society.
I want to give back the help I received to my neighbors.

examples.ko: 복잡한 문제를 하나의 원인으로 환원하면 오해가 생겨요.
examples.en: Reducing a complicated problem to a single cause leads to misunderstanding.
Iron is obtained by reducing iron oxide.
A part of the earnings was given back to the fans.

explain: 환원하다는 얻은 이익이나 도움을 다시 돌려줄 때 '사회에 환원하다'로 가장 많이 써요. '돌려주다'보다 격식이 있고 기부, 나눔의 느낌이 있어요. 과학 시간에는 산소를 떼어 내는 반응을 '환원하다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 성공하면 번 돈을 사회에 환원하고 싶어요.
phrases.en: If I succeed, I want to give the money I earned back to society.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받은 도움이나 이익을 되갚고 싶은 마음을 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connected form for wanting to repay help or profit you received.
phrases.en_equiv: want to give back to society

phrases.en: I want to return the help I received.
phrases.nuance_ko: '환원하다'보다 쉽고 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier than 환원하다 and more natural in daily conversation.

phrases.en: I donated part of the profit to a children's hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: '환원하다'는 돌려준다는 느낌이고, '기부하다'는 돈이나 물건을 대가 없이 내놓는다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 환원하다 feels like giving back, while 기부하다 means giving money or goods without expecting anything.

explain_en: Formal; return profits to community or restore something (수익을 환원하다) Its most common use is '사회에 환원하다', giving back gains or help you received. It is more formal than '돌려주다' (return) and carries a sense of donation and sharing. In science class, it also names the reaction that removes oxygen from a substance.

t90.ax: Iron is obtained by reducing iron oxide.

examples.ko: 이사할 때 가재도구가 많아서 트럭이 두 대 필요했어요.
examples.en: We had so many household goods when moving that we needed two trucks.

examples.ko: 화재로 집의 가재도구가 모두 타 버렸어요.
examples.en: All the household belongings in the house burned in the fire.

examples.ko: 비에 젖은 가재도구를 마당에 널어 말렸어요.
examples.en: We hung the rain-soaked household items in the yard to dry.

examples.ko: 낡은 가재도구를 정리해서 중고 시장에 내놨어요.
examples.en: I sorted out my old household items and put them up on the used market.

examples.ko: 신혼집에 필요한 가재도구를 하나씩 사고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm buying the household items we need for our newlywed home one by one.

examples.ko: 이 보험은 집 안의 가재도구까지 보상해 줘요.
examples.en: This insurance even covers the household goods inside the home.

explain: 집에서 쓰는 가구, 그릇, 옷 같은 살림 물건을 한꺼번에 부르는 말이에요. 이사, 화재, 수해 뉴스에서 자주 나오고, 일상에서는 '살림'이나 '짐'이라고도 해요. 물건 하나하나를 가리킬 때는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: The movers carried our household goods for us.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이사할 때 짐을 나르는 상황에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when moving house and carrying belongings.

phrases.example: 홍수로 집 안의 가재도구가 물에 잠겼어요.
phrases.en: The household goods in the house were flooded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수해 뉴스에서 피해를 말할 때 나오는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase seen in flood news when describing damage.

phrases.en: I threw away a lot of old household things when I moved.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '가재도구' 대신 이 말을 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday talk, people use this more often than 가재도구.

explain_en: Older, formal term for household belongings when moving. It is a collective word for the furniture, dishes, clothes and other things used in a household. It often appears in news about moving, fires and floods, and in daily talk people also say '살림' or '짐'. You don't use it for one single item.

examples.en: They sell household goods on this floor.
I bought the household goods I needed before moving.
Where is the household goods section?
Household goods are very cheap at this store.
If you order household goods all at once, delivery is free.
I looked at cleaning tools at the household goods shop.

explain: 집에서 쓰는 그릇, 청소 도구, 수건 같은 물건을 한꺼번에 부르는 말이에요. 마트나 쇼핑몰의 코너 이름으로 자주 보여요. 큰 가전제품은 보통 '가전'이라고 따로 불러요.

phrases.en: I bought a towel in the household goods section.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마트나 쇼핑몰의 매장 이름으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used as a section name in stores and malls.

phrases.en: I bought cleaning tools at a household goods store.
phrases.nuance_ko: '가정용품'과 비슷하게 쓰고 더 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used much like '가정용품' but more everyday.

phrases.example: 이사 갈 때 필요한 가정용품을 챙겼어요.
phrases.en: I packed the household goods I needed for the move.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집에서 쓸 물건을 준비한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means getting household items ready.

explain_en: It is a collective word for items used at home, such as dishes, cleaning tools and towels. You often see it as a section name in marts and shopping malls. Large appliances are usually called '가전' separately.

en: groundwood paper; coarse paper; newsprint paper

examples.en: There was a time when exam papers were made of coarse paper.
Newsprint is cheap but turns yellow quickly.
The child drew a picture on rough paper with crayons.

examples.ko: 갱지 위에 쓰면 볼펜 글씨가 조금 번져요.
examples.en: If you write on it, ballpoint ink spreads a little on coarse paper.

examples.ko: 할머니는 갱지 공책을 아직 갖고 계세요.
examples.en: My grandmother still has a notebook made of coarse paper.
I bought some coarse paper at the stationery store to use as scrap paper.

explain: 신문지나 옛날 시험지, 연습장처럼 값싸고 거친 종이를 말할 때 써요. 요즘은 '갱지' 하면 옛날 학교 물건이 떠오르는 사람이 많아요. 매끈하고 좋은 종이는 '백상지'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I doodled on the rough paper of my notebook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에'를 붙여 글씨를 쓰는 종이를 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: The particle '에' marks the paper you write on.

phrases.en: The rough-paper test sheet turned yellow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날 학교 시험지를 떠올리게 하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing that recalls old school test sheets.
phrases.en_equiv: test paper made of rough paper

phrases.example: 책상 위에 누런 갱지가 쌓여 있어요.
phrases.en: Yellowed rough paper is piled on the desk.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오래되어 색이 변한 값싼 종이를 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to picture old, cheap paper that has changed color.

explain_en: Cheap coarse paper, once common for exam sheets and old printing. It is used for cheap, rough paper like newsprint, old exam sheets and scrap notebooks. These days many people associate 갱지 with old school days. Smooth, good-quality paper is called '백상지'.

examples.en: The lobby floor is marble, so it's slippery.
The marble stairs sparkled in the sunlight.
This statue is made of white marble.
A marble dining table is pretty but expensive.
I spilled coffee on the marble and a stain was left.
I bought marble-pattern wallpaper and put it up.

explain: 건물 바닥, 조각, 주방 상판처럼 건축과 인테리어에서 자주 나오는 단단한 돌이에요. '대리석 무늬'처럼 진짜 돌이 아니어도 무늬를 말할 때 써요. 비슷한 돌로 '화강암'이 있어요.

phrases.example: 이 벽지는 대리석 무늬라서 고급스러워 보여요.
phrases.en: This wallpaper has a marble pattern, so it looks luxurious.
phrases.nuance_ko: 진짜 돌이 아니어도 무늬만 비슷할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used even when it isn't real stone but only looks like it.

phrases.en: This statue is made of white marble.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료를 말하는 기본 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic form for naming a material.

phrases.en: I installed a marble countertop in the kitchen.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주방이나 식탁 위의 판을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for kitchen or table tops.

explain_en: It is a hard stone that often appears in architecture and interiors, such as floors, sculptures and kitchen countertops. In '대리석 무늬' it describes a pattern even when the material is not real stone. A similar stone is '화강암' (granite).

examples.en: I bought and ate elvan-roasted eggs at the market.

examples.ko: 맥반석 오징어는 고소해서 영화 볼 때 좋아요.
examples.en: Elvan-roasted squid is savory and good for watching movies.
I went to a sauna with elvan stone floors.

examples.ko: 맥반석 위에서 구운 고구마가 정말 달아요.
examples.en: Sweet potatoes roasted on elvan stones are really sweet.
I sweated a lot in the elvan sauna.

examples.ko: 맥반석으로 만든 그릇에 밥을 지어 봤어요.
examples.en: I cooked rice in a pot made of elvan stone.

explain: 일상에서는 '맥반석 계란', '맥반석 오징어'처럼 구이 음식 이름이나 찜질방 간판에서 자주 보여요. 돌 이름이지만 먹거리와 함께 쓰는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: I ate stone-baked eggs at the sauna.
phrases.nuance_ko: 찜질방에서 가장 흔히 보는 먹거리 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common food pairing seen at saunas.

phrases.en: I went to a stone sauna on the weekend and rested.
phrases.nuance_ko: 간판이나 가게 이름에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen on signs and shop names.

phrases.en: This restaurant is famous for its stone-grilled dishes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돌 위에서 굽는 음식을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to food grilled on stone.

explain_en: In daily life you mostly see it in food names like '맥반석 계란' and '맥반석 오징어', or on sauna signs. It is a stone name, but often appears with food.

examples.ko: 할머니는 본채에서 주무시고 저는 별채에서 자요.
examples.en: Grandmother sleeps in the main building, and I sleep in the annex.

examples.ko: 손님이 오면 본채 거실에서 같이 식사해요.
examples.en: When guests come, we eat together in the living room of the main building.

examples.ko: 이 한옥은 본채가 오래돼서 수리를 많이 했어요.
examples.en: The main building of this hanok is old, so it has had a lot of repairs.

examples.ko: 본채와 별채 사이에 작은 마당이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small yard between the main building and the annex.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와서 본채 지붕이 새기 시작했어요.
examples.en: It rained a lot, and the roof of the main building started to leak.

examples.ko: 저쪽 문으로 들어가면 본채가 바로 나와요.
examples.en: If you go in through that gate, you come right to the main building.

explain: 한 집터 안에 건물이 여러 채 있을 때 중심이 되는 집을 말해요. 짝말은 '별채'이고, 한옥이나 시골집 이야기에서 주로 나와요.

phrases.example: 이 한옥은 본채와 별채가 마당을 사이에 두고 있어요.
phrases.en: In this hanok, the main building and the annex face each other across the yard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 짝말인 '별채'와 함께 써서 집의 구조를 설명할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with '별채', it is often used to describe how a house is laid out.

phrases.en: In winter it's cold, so everyone stays in the main building.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에서'를 붙여 어느 건물에서 생활하는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '에서' it says which building people live in.
phrases.en_equiv: to stay in the main building

phrases.en: The children run around in the front yard of the main building.
phrases.nuance_ko: 본채를 기준으로 주변 장소를 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for places around the main building.
phrases.en_equiv: front yard of the main house

explain_en: When a property has several buildings, this is the central house. Its counterpart is '별채' (annex), and it mostly comes up when talking about hanok or country houses.

examples.ko: 이 가방에는 떼어 낼 수 있는 부속물이 많아요.
examples.en: This bag has many attachments you can detach.

examples.ko: 건물의 부속물까지 모두 계약에 포함돼 있어요.
examples.en: Even the attached fixtures of the building are included in the contract.
The shed in the yard is also an appurtenance of the house.

examples.ko: 건물 부속물을 고치는 비용은 집주인이 내요.
examples.en: The landlord pays to repair the building's attached structures.

examples.ko: 설명서에 부속물 목록이 자세히 나와 있어요.
examples.en: The manual lists the attachments in detail.
The annex looks bigger than the main building.

explain: '부속품'은 기계에 딸린 작은 물건에 주로 쓰고, '부속물'은 본채에 딸린 창고나 마당 시설처럼 주된 것에 붙은 것까지 넓게 가리켜요. 건물이나 계약 이야기에서 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.example: 이 집에는 창고 같은 부속물이 딸려 있어요.
phrases.en: This house comes with attachments like a storage shed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주된 건물에 함께 붙어 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means something comes along with the main building.

phrases.en: The price includes all the attachments too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계약이나 가격 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about contracts or prices.

phrases.en: Please take off the attachments before cleaning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 붙어 있는 것을 분리할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when detaching something that is attached.

explain_en: '부속품' is mostly for small items that go with a machine, while '부속물' covers anything attached to a main thing, such as a shed or yard facilities next to a house. It appears more often in talk about buildings and contracts.

t90.ax: The manual lists the attachments in detail.

examples.ko: 이 방에는 붙박이 옷장이 있어서 편해요.
examples.en: This room has a built-in wardrobe, which is convenient.
I'm looking for a house with built-in closets.

examples.ko: 새 집에는 붙박이 책장이 벽 전체에 있어요.
examples.en: The new house has a built-in bookshelf covering the whole wall.

examples.ko: 붙박이 가구는 이사할 때 가져갈 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't take built-in furniture with you when you move.

examples.ko: 삼촌은 우리 동네 카페의 붙박이 손님이에요.
examples.en: My uncle is a regular fixture at the café in our neighborhood.

examples.ko: 싱크대 옆에 수납장을 붙박이로 짜 넣었어요.
examples.en: We built a storage cabinet in next to the sink.

explain: 집에서는 벽에 맞춰 짜 넣어 옮길 수 없는 '붙박이장', '붙박이 가구'로 써요. 비유로 한 자리를 늘 차지하는 사람에도 써서 '붙박이 주전'처럼 말해요. 옮길 수 있는 가구는 그냥 '가구'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 삼 년째 대표팀의 붙박이 주전이에요.
phrases.en: That player has been a permanent starter on the national team for three years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감독이 늘 선발로 쓰는, 자리가 정해진 선수를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a player whose starting spot is always secure with the coach.

explain_en: At home it is used for things built to fit the wall and can't be moved, as in '붙박이장' or '붙박이 가구'. It is also used figuratively for a person who always holds one spot, as in '붙박이 주전'. Furniture you can move is simply called '가구'.

en: to be densely packed; to be crowded

examples.ko: 중개 사무소 앞에는 매물 정보가 빼곡히 붙어 있어요.
examples.en: Property listings are packed tightly on the wall in front of the real estate office.

examples.ko: 달력에 약속이 빼곡해서 시간을 내기 어려워요.
examples.en: My calendar is packed with appointments, so it's hard to find time.
Our bookshelf is crammed full of books.

examples.ko: 빼곡한 일정 때문에 점심도 못 먹었어요.
examples.en: Because of the packed schedule, I couldn't even eat lunch.
I filled the notebook with tightly written text.
The subway is jam-packed with people at rush hour.

explain: '빽빽하다'처럼 빈틈없이 꽉 찬 모습이에요. 일정, 글씨, 책, 사람처럼 작은 것이 많이 들어찰 때 쓰고, 부사 '빼곡히'와 '빼곡하게' 형태로 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: The books are packed tightly on the bookshelf.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사에서 나온 부사로, 빈틈없이 가득 찬 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form, describing a space filled with no gaps.

phrases.example: 이번 주는 빼곡한 일정 때문에 정신이 없어요.
phrases.en: This week is hectic because of a packed schedule.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 쓰는 형태로, 일정이 꽉 찼다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used before a noun, meaning the schedule is full.

phrases.en: The writing is so dense that it is hard to read.
phrases.nuance_ko: '빼곡하다'와 거의 같고, 일상에서 더 흔히 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same as 빼곡하다 and more common in everyday speech.

explain_en: Like '빽빽하다', it shows something filled to the brim with no gaps. It is used when many small things are packed in, such as schedules, writing, books or people, and often appears as the adverbs '빼곡히' and '빼곡하게'.

t90.ax: Our bookshelf is crammed full of books.

examples.en: A blue sapphire is set in the engagement ring.
Sapphires are usually blue.
My grandmother passed down a sapphire necklace to me.
I received sapphire earrings as a gift from a friend.

examples.ko: 이 사파이어는 크기가 커서 값이 비싸요.
examples.en: This sapphire is large, so it's expensive.
The birthstone for people born in September is the sapphire.

explain: '사파이어'는 파란색이 대표적이라 '사파이어 블루'처럼 색 이름으로도 써요. 붉은 보석인 '루비'와 짝으로 같이 나올 때가 많아요. 서양에서 들어온 보석 이름은 대부분 외래어 그대로 써요.

phrases.en: My mother is wearing a sapphire ring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사파이어로 만든 반지를 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A very common pairing for a ring set with sapphire.

phrases.example: 사파이어 목걸이가 파란 드레스와 잘 어울려요.
phrases.en: The sapphire necklace goes well with the blue dress.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보석 이름 뒤에 장신구 이름을 붙여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Name the gem first, then the accessory.

phrases.en: The sea sparkles in sapphire blue.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깊고 진한 파란색을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a deep, rich blue color.

explain_en: Blue is the typical color, so '사파이어' is also used as a color name, as in '사파이어 블루'. It often appears as a pair with the red gem '루비' (ruby). Gem names that came from the West are mostly used as loanwords.

examples.en: The front gate is tied up with a chain.
The puppy was tied to a chain.
I locked my bike to the post with a chain.
The chain was so heavy that my hands sweated.
In the movie the prisoner was wearing chains.
The chain rusted and snapped.

explain: 쇠사슬은 쇠고리를 이어서 만든 줄이에요. '체인'과 같은 뜻이지만 자전거 체인이나 가게 이름 같은 곳에서는 '체인'을 더 많이 써요. 자유를 막는 것을 비유로 말할 때는 '사슬'이나 '속박'을 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: I locked the door tightly with a chain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '쇠사슬'을 줄인 말처럼 쓰고, 비유로도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It works like a short form of 쇠사슬 and is also often used figuratively.

phrases.en: The dog broke the chain and ran outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: '끊다'와 함께 써서 묶여 있던 것에서 풀려나는 장면을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With 끊다 it describes breaking free from something tied up.

phrases.en: The bicycle chain came off, so I need to fix it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기계 부품이나 가게 이름에는 영어에서 온 '체인'을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For machine parts and shop names, the English loanword 체인 is more common.

explain_en: Native word for a heavy metal chain, used to bind (자전거를 튼튼한 쇠사슬로 기둥에 묶어 두었어요.) 쇠사슬 is a line made of linked metal rings. It means the same as '체인', but for bike chains or store chains people mostly say '체인'. For something that restricts freedom, '사슬' or '속박' are used figuratively.

examples.en: I cut out articles I like and paste them in a scrapbook.
I made a scrapbook with my travel photos.
My daughter stuck lots of stickers in her scrapbook.
My scrapbook is full of movie tickets.

examples.ko: 스크랩북 한 권이 벌써 다 찼어요.
examples.en: One scrapbook is already full.
I decorated a scrapbook with care to give to my teacher.

explain: 기사, 사진, 티켓 같은 것을 오려 붙여 모으는 공책이에요. '스크랩하다'는 신문이나 자료를 오려 모으는 동작을 말하는 동사로, 스크랩북에 붙이기 전 단계예요.

phrases.en: I made a scrapbook after the trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스크랩북을 직접 꾸밀 때 쓰는 가장 기본적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for making one yourself.

phrases.en: I stuck the ticket in my scrapbook.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모은 것을 공책에 붙이는 동작이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The action of pasting collected things into the book.

phrases.en: I clip articles that I like.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스크랩북에 붙이기 전에 오려 모으는 동작이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The step of cutting and collecting before pasting into the book.

explain_en: It is a notebook where you paste clippings, photos or tickets. The verb '스크랩하다' names the earlier step of cutting out and saving articles or materials before pasting them in.
